This will not hide `end_bone_name`
should `end_bone_name` should be inside `end_bone` (`end_bone/name`)?

The setters behave differently depending on whether `get_skeleton()` is null.

I am worried there are cases which can desynchronize bone name/index
Does this serialize both bone_name and bone (index)? I think we should pick one. We should only serialize bone_name.
I think this should only run if `extend_end_bone` (since the property is undefined if not `extend_end_bone`)

I was surprised that this function does not directly call `_update_joints`, but it does not always need to.

It is confusing that `_skeleton_changed` in the subclass calls `_make_all_joints_dirty` which calls `_update_joints`.

This function calls `set_root_bone_name` which sometimes calls `set_root_bone` which sometimes calls `_update_joints`

The ordering and conditions for these update functions is quite complex for me to analyze. I would prefer if this flow is simpler and easier to understand. For example: when property is changed, if the skeleton is not null; or else the virtual functions when skeleton is changed (or _validate_bone_names)

Using both the bone name and index inherits the design of BoneAttachment. All other SkeletonModifier bone settings are serialized in the same way.

I remember discussing this with @fire in the past, and the main reasons for this design were to maintain compatibility with BoneAttachment and prevent glTF reimporting from breaking the indices (by making priority with the names).

It might be possible to remove this in the future, like in Godot5, but we should maintain consistency at least throughout Godot4. Therefore, this should not be changed in this PR.

If we want to change this, we should send a PR later that changes all other Nodes for Skeleton at the same time.
Same as below https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110120#discussion_r2462824011

The joint update logic uses nearly the same approach as SpringBoneSimulator3D.

The differences from SpringBoneSimulator3D are the use of a base class and the method for extending the struct array. However, the struct array-related methods adopted in this PR also reuse the design from the already-merged BoneConstraint3D.

In other words, it combines the designs of BoneConstraint3D and SpringBoneSimulator3D; this implementation is not being adopted for the first time in this PR.

What's slightly unique is that, unlike BoneConstraint3D, it requires an init process. Therefore, a virtual function is needed in the base class to call the init function for each struct array with different structs.

However, I couldn't find a better way to handle struct array properties with differing structures rather than current way.

This is due to conflicts between templates and inheritance. Considering compatibility with Godot's property registration, templates cannot be used extensively, making this approach necessary. Using Resources instead of Structs is another option, but it's probably not advisable from a performance and complexity standpoint.

To achieve cleaner code through other means would likely involve duplicating most of the init-related code across each class. However, this is essentially equivalent to splitting the ManyBoneIK class into five non-inherited classes, which I believe should not be done.

---

The only other conceivable approach might be to define the struct as a separate class outside ManyBoneIK and handle struct inheritance outside ManyBoneIK, which could potentially make things a bit cleaner.

However, since it didn't seem like many nodes would require a dedicated class for structs outside the class, I hesitated and settled on the current implementation.

When time permits, it might be worth trying that approach later. And I believe it can be dealt with as a follow-up PR that doesn't break compatibility if it works better.
